articles.title: Bombeiros buscam quatro desaparecidos no Cânion Tajuvas, no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Dois dos desaparecidos seriam mãe e filho, segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros. Os outros dois, um homem e uma mulher. As idades seriam de 47 anos, 15 anos, 41 anos e 38 anos. As identidades não foram divulgadas.
articles.summary: As equipes de buscas utilizam drones e cães, e com equipes do batalhão de busca e salvamento de Porto Alegre. Dois dos desaparecidos seriam mãe e filho, segundo os bombeiros.
articles.body:
Bombeiros buscam desaparecidos no Cânion Tajuvas, no RS — Foto: CBM-RS/Divulgação

O Corpo de Bombeiros do Rio Grande do Sul busca quatro desaparecidos no Cânion Tajuvas, em Morrinhos do Sul , município de 3 mil habitantes a 180 quilômetros de Porto Alegre . O mau tempo dificulta os trabalhos das autoridades: há neblina e chuva no local.

Nesta segunda-feira (31), as equipes de buscas de Torres, no Litoral Norte, utilizam drones e cães, e contam com auxílio de profissionais do batalhão de busca e salvamento de Porto Alegre.

Dois dos desaparecidos seriam mãe e filho, segundo os bombeiros. Os outros dois, um homem e uma mulher. As idades seriam de 47 anos, 15 anos, 41 anos e 38 anos. As identidades não foram divulgadas.

Conforme a secretária de Turismo de Morrinhos do Sul, Jucelaine Medeiros, as buscas começaram no domingo (30) de tarde.

"Está bem complicado no local, com neblina e chuva. Agora que conseguimos estabelecer uma internet móvel lá. Caso contrário, sequer tem sinal telefônico", afirma Thiago Bona, capitão do Corpo de Bombeiros.

Conforme ocorrência do Corpo de Bombeiros, o grupo era formado inicialmente por quatro pessoas. Eles teriam um guia turístico, que teria dito a eles que retornassem em razão das condições climáticas.

O guia retornou e informou às autoridades: nesse contato foi relatado que os quatro têm mantimentos, como comida e água.

Segundo Nilvia Pinto Pereira, dona do Recanto Sobragi, que fica em Morrinhos do Sul, o grupo começou o trekking pelos cânions Tajuvas, Josafaz e Pedras Brancas e pernoitou no Cânion Tajuvas, de sábado (29) para domingo:

"Na manhã de domingo, devido à chuva, neblina e baixa visibilidade, o condutor (guia) orientou todos a interromper a travessia e descer. Quatro participantes seguiram por conta própria. As operações seguem em condições climáticas muito adversas, com chuva, frio, neblina intensa."

articles.title: Jaborandi Geek Fest reúne tecnologia, games e cultura geek | G1
articles.standfirst: Realizado pela Prefeitura de Jaborandi e pelo CTech, evento reuniu tecnologia, games, cosplay e atrações especiais, com apoio de instituições e municípios da região.
articles.summary: Realizado pela Prefeitura de Jaborandi e pelo CTech, evento reuniu tecnologia, games, cosplay e atrações especiais, com apoio de instituições e municípios da região.
articles.body:
Jaborandi Geek Fest reúne tecnologia, games e cultura geek — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

Jaborandi recebeu uma programação dedicada à cultura geek, à tecnologia e aos games com a realização do Jaborandi Geek Fest, promovido pela Prefeitura de Jaborandi e pelo CTech.

O evento contou com o apoio da Prefeitura de Barretos, Prefeitura de Colina, Prefeitura de Morro Agudo, Senac e Goblin School, reunindo diferentes parceiros em uma programação voltada a públicos de diversas idades.

Com duração de 10 horas, das 9h às 19h, o Geek Fest foi planejado para oferecer experiências relacionadas à tecnologia, aos jogos e ao entretenimento.

Entre as atrações estiveram exposições tecnológicas, workshops, cosplays, pilotagem de drones, oficina de escultura, feira geek e sala de games. O evento também contou com uma praça de alimentação personalizada.

Dubladoras de “Encanto” participaram do evento

Um dos destaques da programação foi a participação das artistas dubladoras do filme “Encanto”, da Disney , Veridiana Benassi, responsável pela voz da personagem Tia Pepa, e Mariana Evangelista, que interpreta Maribel na versão brasileira.

Os fãs tiveram a oportunidade de participar de um Meet & Greet com as dubladoras, podendo conhecê-las pessoalmente e registrar o encontro com fotografias.

A participação das artistas acrescentou à programação uma experiência voltada aos fãs de animação, cinema e dublagem, aproximando o público de profissionais ligados à produção.

A programação do Jaborandi Geek Fest reuniu diferentes áreas do universo geek e tecnológico. As atividades incluíram experiências com tecnologia, pilotagem de drones, jogos, cosplay, oficinas e feira especializada.

A proposta permitiu que o público tivesse contato com diferentes formas de entretenimento e aprendizado em um mesmo espaço, aproximando tecnologia, criatividade e cultura pop.

A participação do CTech , centro tecnológico de Jaborandi, também reforçou a presença da inovação na programação, conectando o evento às iniciativas de tecnologia desenvolvidas no município.

A realização do evento contou com a colaboração de instituições e administrações municipais da região. O apoio das Prefeituras de Barretos, Colina e Morro Agudo, além do Senac e da Goblin School, contribuiu para ampliar a programação e fortalecer a integração regional em torno da tecnologia e da cultura geek.

A parceria entre diferentes organizações também demonstra o potencial de iniciativas que aproximam educação, tecnologia, entretenimento e criatividade.

A participação de parlamentares se somou à presença dos municípios e instituições parceiras, reforçando a importância do evento para a região e para a valorização de iniciativas relacionadas à tecnologia, educação e cultura geek.

O Jaborandi Geek Fest foi pensado para todos os públicos e diferentes faixas etárias , reunindo crianças, jovens, adultos e famílias em torno de atividades relacionadas aos games, tecnologia e cultura pop.

Além da programação de entretenimento, o evento proporcionou novas experiências ao público por meio de oficinas, exposições e atividades práticas.

Com a realização da Prefeitura de Jaborandi e do CTech, e o apoio de instituições e municípios da região, o Geek Fest se consolidou como uma iniciativa que aproxima a comunidade de tecnologia, criatividade, games e cultura geek , criando um espaço de convivência e novas experiências para o público.

articles.title: Família do Nepal foge de avalanche antes de casa ser arrastada | G1
articles.standfirst: Desastre no Himalaia já fez quase mil mortos e deixou mais de 4,5 mil desaparecidos.
articles.summary: Desastre no Himalaia já fez quase mil mortos e deixou mais de 4,5 mil desaparecidos.
articles.body:
Um vídeo da avalanche que devastou a fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete, na China , mostra o desespero de uma família que escapou por pouco da enxurrada de lama e detritos, na última quarta-feira (26).

Nas imagens, uma mulher corre segurando duas crianças pelas mãos, momentos antes de virar-se para ver sua casa ser arrastada pela força da água.

O vídeo também mostra os nepaleses espantados diante da catástrofe natural que soterrou milhares de casas e destruiu plantações. Alguns fogem às pressas na direção contrária da avalanche.

A tragédia deixou mais de 900 mortos e mais de 4,5 mil desaparecidos - entre eles, turistas e peregrinos que viajavam em direção ao Monte Kailash , considerado sagrado e localizado na região autônoma chinesa do Tibete .

O número de cidadãos estrangeiros desaparecidos está em 590. Até o momento, os corpos de 323 estrangeiros foram resgatados.

O Nepal começou nesta segunda-feira (31) a sepultar parte dos corpos recuperados após a avalanche que provocou uma enorme onda de gelo, pedras e detritos no Himalaia.

Vídeo mostra o desespero de uma família fugindo da enxurrada que atingiu o Nepal momentos antes de sua casa ser arrastada pelas águas — Foto: Reprodução: Redes Sociais

articles.title: Tamil Nadu announces major housing reforms, Rs 2,883 crore plan to rebuild flats
articles.summary: News News: Tamil Nadu minister B Rajkumar on Friday announced a series of initiatives aimed at streamlining building approvals, digitising land-use processes, ex.
articles.body: Tamil Nadu minister B Rajkumar on Friday announced a series of initiatives aimed at streamlining building approvals, digitising land-use processes, expanding self-certification and providing financial relief to housing borrowers.Speaking during the debate on the demands for grants for his department in the Assembly, the housing and urban development minister also announced a Rs 2,882.62 crore plan to reconstruct 12,648 dilapidated flats across 20 project areas.Land-use applications to go fully digitalThe Directorate of Town and Country Planning will digitise the entire process for land-use change applications, the minister said.Self-certification will be expanded to cover residential buildings of up to 5,000 sq ft. The facility will also be introduced for small commercial buildings of up to 1,500 sq ft.Third-party certification will be introduced for:Commercial buildings of up to 3,230 sq ftResidential buildings of up to 8,070 sq ftIndustrial structures of up to 26,900 sq ft in approved SIDCO, SIPCOT and ELCOT layoutsLocal body approval limits raisedRajkumar said local body approval limits for residential projects would be increased to 16,140 sq ft for corporations and municipalities and 12,912 sq ft for town and village panchayats.“Commercial approval limits for all local bodies will increase to 5,380 sq ft, while procedures for reclassifying wet agricultural land in non-planned areas will also be streamlined through multi-departmental clearances,” he said.Rs 2,883 crore plan to rebuild dilapidated flatsThe Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board (TNUHDB) plans to reconstruct 12,648 dilapidated flats across 20 project areas at a cost of Rs 2,882.62 crore.The demolition of 9,918 unsafe units will be taken up first, the minister said.The board will also spend:Rs 96.63 crore to renovate 41,664 old flatsRs 355 crore to upgrade civic infrastructure across 208 housing sitesRs 75 lakh to launch an integrated Smart Habitat Management PlatformInterest relief for housing borrowersFor primary cooperative housing societies, the government will introduce a broad interest-waiver scheme for borrowers who have defaulted on repayments.The scheme will also provide an additional one percentage point interest waiver for borrowers in the Low Income Group and Middle Income Group categories, Rajkumar said.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Watch: Drone accidentally captures catastrophic avalanche on Mount Langtang in Nepal
articles.summary: South Asia News: A Chinese photographer accidentally captured the moment a massive ice-rock avalanche struck Mount Langtang Lirung in Nepal during a drone shoot on Aug.
articles.body: A Chinese photographer accidentally captured the moment a massive ice-rock avalanche struck Mount Langtang Lirung in Nepal during a drone shoot on August 26. This has offered researchers new clues about the disaster that triggered a deadly chain of floods and landslides in the Himalayas.The footage, recorded from a mountaintop radar station in China, shows a white mass suddenly cascading down the mountain, followed by a huge brown dust cloud rising from the Lhende Khola Valley, according to a report by Nepal Times.According to the analysis, the disaster appears to have been caused not simply by a glacier collapse but by the failure of the mountain's rock face beneath a hanging glacier. A massive combination of rock and ice then plunged about 1,500 metres down the north face before crashing onto the glacier below.The impact triggered a 5.2-magnitude tremor and sent a torrent of debris and water into the river system. The resulting mudflow reportedly reached the Chinese customs and immigration building in Gyirong within about 20 minutes before travelling downstream towards the Trisuli valley.Scientists are studying the newly emerged footage to better understand what triggered the collapse and identify similar risks elsewhere in the Himalayas. Researchers have pointed to the region's fragile geology and warming temperatures, which can thaw permafrost that helps bind mountain rock together.The footage has emerged as Nepal continues rescue and rehabilitation efforts following the wider disaster.The death toll climbed to 903 on Monday, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), while around 4,247 people remain missing. articles.title: A Tennessee man left a late-1700s house and about $500,000 to local government for a park; after nearly a decade of delays, the property and money are going to a descendant
articles.summary: US News: A historic late-18th-century home and about $500,000 in cash given to a local Tennessee government to create a public park have been returned to a fam.
articles.body: A historic late-18th-century home and about $500,000 in cash given to a local Tennessee government to create a public park have been returned to a family descendant after nearly 10 years of municipal delays. The legal transfer ends a long dispute over the estate, which was originally meant to protect local history and create open green space for the community. According to a report published by AOL, the local authority failed to meet important deadlines and responsibilities set out in the owner's will. As a result, a legal process returned both the property and the money to the owner's family. The property includes a house built in the late 1700s, making it a rare surviving example of early settlement architecture in the region. When the owner died nearly a decade ago, the will clearly stated that the home and surrounding land should be turned into a public park. A $500,000 endowment was also provided to pay for early improvements, preparing the site and future maintenance.A vision delayed by local governmentLocal officials initially accepted the gift with enthusiasm, but struggled to turn the owner's plans into reality. The project remained stalled through several municipal administrations because of bureaucracy, changing council priorities and concerns about liability and future maintenance costs. As the years passed without major work at the site, the late-1700s house remained empty and exposed to the elements. Rain, wind and other weather conditions damaged the original timber siding, stonework and structural frame. Heritage advocates became increasingly worried that the building could suffer serious and permanent damage before the planned park ever opened. At the same time, the $500,000 endowment remained unused in municipal accounts. Local officials had not approved a final master plan or restoration programme, leaving the money untouched while the historic property continued to deteriorate.Conditions written into the original giftThe estate documents described in the AOL report made clear that the donation was not unconditional. Under Tennessee property and probate law, gifts of property to public bodies can include reversion clauses. These clauses can require the property to return to the original estate or named heirs if the government receiving it fails to meet the main conditions of the gift within a set or reasonable period. After almost 10 years without the promised public park being created, legal representatives for the estate and a direct descendant began court proceedings to enforce the terms of the will. Court records showed that the local government could not provide a clear timeline, funding plan or operating strategy that met the requirements set by the former owner. Probate authorities therefore found that the conditions of the trust had been broken because of the long period of inaction.Family takes control of historic homeAfter the court's final decision, legal control of both the historic house and the $500,000 fund was transferred to the descendant. The decision removed the local council's responsibility for the property and returned the task of protecting the historic home to the family. The descendant has now taken charge of the preservation work and plans to stabilise the building before further damage occurs. Unlike the local government, which had to deal with public procurement rules, competitive bidding and other municipal spending priorities, the private owner can move more quickly to hire specialists in historic restoration. The $500,000 fund has also been transferred with the property. It is expected to be used for urgent repairs, including protecting the timber, strengthening the foundation and repairing the roof.What the case shows about donated historic propertiesThe Tennessee estate highlights a wider problem that can occur when individuals leave historic properties to local governments. Such gifts are often made to benefit the public, but smaller municipalities may not have the staff, preservation experts or long-term funding needed to care for old buildings. Without officials willing to keep the project moving or strong political support, conditional property gifts can become difficult and expensive responsibilities for local councils. Local governments must also balance historic preservation with other urgent needs, including road repairs, public safety and improvements to water and other public services. When delays continue for years, reversion clauses in wills can provide an important legal safeguard. They help prevent historic properties from remaining stuck in government offices and unused for an indefinite period.Restoration now becomes the priorityLocal historians who followed the dispute have welcomed the court decision and said the focus should now move from legal and administrative issues to protecting the building itself. Although the property will no longer become a public park as the deceased owner originally intended, the goal of preserving a rare piece of 18th-century Tennessee architecture may now be easier to achieve under family ownership. Initial work is expected to begin after building permits and structural engineering assessments are completed. The descendant plans to first protect the house from rain, pests and further weather damage before deciding how the restored property and surrounding land could be used in the future. The final court orders have removed the local government's remaining responsibilities for the estate, bringing nearly a decade of delays to an end and giving the historic home a new chance at survival.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Michigan’s AQI hit 616 after Ontario wildfire smoke crossed into the US; scientists warn a warming climate could make such pollution more common
articles.summary: US News: Smoke from Canadian wildfires can travel hundreds or even thousands of kilometres, turning a distant fire into a serious air-quality emergency. That d.
articles.body: Smoke from Canadian wildfires can travel hundreds or even thousands of kilometres, turning a distant fire into a serious air-quality emergency. That danger was starkly illustrated when wildfire smoke from Ontario moved into the United States and contributed to exceptionally poor air quality across parts of the Midwest. In Michigan, the Air Quality Index reportedly reached an extraordinary 616, a level far beyond the EPA’s hazardous category. But the episode is part of a much larger concern. Scientists have increasingly linked worsening wildfire conditions with a warming climate, while new research shows that smoke-derived fine particulate pollution is already contributing substantially to premature deaths across the United States. A 2026 Science Advances study estimated that wildfire-smoke PM2.5 was responsible for approximately 24,100 deaths each year in the contiguous US between 2006 and 2020.How wildfire smoke from Ontario reached MichiganWildfire smoke does not remain close to the flames that produce it. Once fine particles enter the atmosphere, winds and large-scale weather systems can carry them across state and national borders, exposing communities far from the original fires. Research published in The Lancet Planetary Health has shown that wildfire smoke can affect regions far beyond the areas where fires are burning, including the US Midwest through long-range transport. Michigan’s extreme air-quality episode demonstrates how quickly this distant pollution can become a local problem. Smoke transported from Canadian fires can contain high concentrations of fine particulate matter, or PM2.5, which is small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs. The particles can also enter the bloodstream, making wildfire smoke considerably more dangerous than simply an unpleasant haze. The scale of the pollution is particularly concerning because communities do not need to experience a wildfire directly to face its consequences. A fire burning hundreds of kilometres away can produce an air-quality emergency when atmospheric conditions carry its emissions towards populated areas. Scientists have therefore increasingly treated wildfire smoke as a continent-wide environmental and public-health issue. As fire seasons become more severe in some regions, the areas exposed to smoke can expand well beyond traditional wildfire zones.Why PM2.5 from wildfire smoke is a serious health threatThe most significant pollutant in wildfire smoke is PM2.5, referring to particles with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 micrometres or smaller. Their tiny size allows them to travel deep into the respiratory system, where prolonged exposure can contribute to harmful health effects. A 2026 study in Science Advances, examining the contiguous United States between 2006 and 2020, found that wildfire-smoke PM2.5 was associated with increased mortality across the outcomes studied. The researchers estimated that wildfire smoke was responsible for approximately 24,100 all-cause deaths per year. Importantly, their analysis found no evidence of a clear “safe” threshold for the relationship between smoke PM2.5 exposure and mortality. Earlier research has similarly demonstrated that long-term exposure can have consequences beyond the immediate respiratory irritation often associated with smoky conditions. A study examining 2007–2020 data estimated approximately 11,415 non-accidental deaths annually were attributable to long-term wildfire-smoke PM2.5 exposure. These findings make extreme AQI events more than a temporary inconvenience. They represent one visible manifestation of a much broader exposure problem, particularly as wildfire smoke increasingly affects densely populated areas outside traditional fire-prone regions.Climate change is intensifying the wildfire smoke problemHealth impacts have a strong link with the changing dynamics of wildfires and the climate. It has been discovered that human-induced climate change has expanded the forest-fire area in temperate and boreal North America due to increasing warm and dry weather, which helps make a suitable environment for fires. A study conducted in the contiguous United States from 2006 to 2020 indicated that climate change was responsible for around 15,000 deaths from pollution due to wildfires during 15 years. The researchers also estimated an associated economic burden of around $160 billion, warning that the health effects of climate-driven wildfire smoke are expected to increase without major changes in climate trajectories and land management. Another major study, ‘Wildfire smoke exposure and mortality burden in the USA under climate change’ published in Nature modelled how wildfire-smoke exposure could change under future warming. Researchers projected that smoke PM2.5 could cause approximately 71,420 excess deaths per year by 2050 under a high-warming scenario, representing a 73% increase compared with the estimated 2011–2020 annual average. The same research estimated that cumulative excess deaths from wildfire smoke could reach 1.9 million between 2026 and 2055 under that high-warming scenario. The researchers also found evidence that mortality impacts associated with smoke exposure can persist for as long as three years after exposure.Wildfire smoke could become a growing US air pollution threatThe changing wildfire landscape creates a difficult challenge for US air-quality policy. Decades of pollution controls have reduced many conventional sources of particulate pollution, but wildfire emissions can undermine some of those gains. The wildfire smoke contributed to changes in US PM2.5 trends, particularly in wildfire-prone regions. The threat is also becoming increasingly widespread. The Nature study also found that wildfire-smoke PM2.5 exposure could increase substantially under future climate scenarios, with neighbouring and downwind populations facing particularly significant increases. For states such as Michigan, the lesson from severe Canadian smoke episodes is clear, wildfire preparedness is no longer solely a concern for communities living near forests that frequently burn. Air-quality alerts, access to clean indoor air and public awareness can become increasingly important when smoke travels across borders. The Michigan episode therefore offers a glimpse of a wider challenge. As climate change alters wildfire conditions, the smoke generated by those fires could become an increasingly important source of air pollution across the United States, with consequences extending far beyond the flames themselves. The original research suggests that limiting this growing burden will require both better protection against smoke exposure and efforts to address the climatic and land-management conditions that are helping drive increasingly severe fires.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Pacific island’s coconut plantations became an “avian desert”; scientists say native vegetation must return after rats are removed
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Across tropical islands in the Pacific and Indian Ocean, the arrival of people brought more than permanent settlements. Forests were cleared, invasive.
articles.body: Across tropical islands in the Pacific and Indian Ocean, the arrival of people brought more than permanent settlements. Forests were cleared, invasive predators were introduced, and large areas were converted into coconut plantations for commercial production. On some islands, the coconut industry eventually declined, but the plantations remained, leaving behind dense stands of a single introduced crop where native forests and grasslands once grew. For seabirds, that legacy can be particularly damaging. On islands where abandoned coconut plantations coexist with invasive rats, the landscape can become what researchers describe as an "avian desert", an area offering little suitable habitat for breeding birds even when food may still be available offshore. A new study titled Potential benefits to breeding seabirds of converting abandoned coconut plantations to native habitats after invasive predator eradication, led by scientists from the Zoological Society of London's Institute of Zoology, together with researchers from the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, the University of Exeter and Heriot-Watt University, examined whether removing rats is enough to reverse that damage. Their results suggest that it is not. If conservationists want heavily degraded tropical islands to support large seabird colonies again, removing invasive predators may need to be accompanied by a much more ambitious step: replacing abandoned coconut plantations with native vegetation.How scientists spent more than a decade studying seabirds across the Chagos ArchipelagoThe research was based on an unusually extensive dataset from the Chagos Archipelago in the central Indian Ocean. Over more than a decade, researchers surveyed the islands and recorded breeding seabirds alongside the habitats in which they nested. The work covered all 55 islands in the archipelago, allowing the researchers to compare islands with different combinations of vegetation and rat presence. That comparison was important because rats are among the most damaging invasive species on oceanic islands. They can eat seabird eggs and chicks and, in some cases, attack adult birds. Removing them can therefore produce an immediate improvement in breeding conditions. But the researchers wanted to know whether the absence of rats automatically meant an island could return to being a major seabird breeding site. The answer depended heavily on vegetation. The team used the field data to model what could happen under several restoration scenarios. The first involved removing rats while leaving the island's existing vegetation largely unchanged. A second model combined rat eradication with restoring the island's vegetation so that it resembled nearby rat-free reference islands. A third went further, assuming that one square kilometre of former coconut plantation would be converted into an equal mixture of native forest and savannah. The three scenarios produced dramatically different estimates, showing that the number of seabirds an island could eventually support depends not just on whether invasive predators are removed, but on what kind of habitat is left behind.Why restoring one Chagos island could produce hundreds of thousands of breeding pairsThe researchers used Ile du Coin, in the Peros Banhos atoll, as an example of what a restored island could look like. At 1.26 square kilometres, it is the fourth-largest island in the Chagos Archipelago. Today, Ile du Coin has rats and is overwhelmingly dominated by former coconut plantations. Around 92% of its vegetation consists of this plantation habitat. Only 51 breeding seabird pairs were recorded on the island, representing three relatively generalist species: Brown Noddies, Lesser Noddies and Common White Terns. The modelling showed what a difference restoration could make. Under a scenario involving rat eradication alongside the existing habitat conditions, the island's projected seabird population rose to roughly 4,306 breeding pairs across 14 species.The researchers then modelled what would happen if rats were eradicated and the island's vegetation was restored to resemble nearby rat-free reference islands. Under that scenario, the model estimated 138,878 breeding pairs within the study's modelling framework. The largest projection came from the most intensive habitat-conversion scenario. Researchers assumed that one square kilometre of the island's abandoned coconut plantation would be replaced by 0.5 square kilometres of native forest and 0.5 square kilometres of native savannah, alongside rat eradication. Under those conditions, the model projected approximately 319,762 breeding pairs across 16 species. The figure is striking because it would make a single restored island capable of supporting an enormous seabird population. It also shows why there is a substantial difference between removing an invasive predator and rebuilding an island's underlying habitat.Why getting rid of rats does not automatically bring back seabirdsRats are an obvious problem because their presence can directly prevent seabirds from successfully raising young. But removing them addresses only one part of the ecological damage. Abandoned coconut plantations can remain difficult environments for native wildlife long after commercial farming has ended. They are often structurally and botanically very different from the native vegetation they replaced. For seabirds, that can mean fewer suitable places to nest and less of the habitat diversity associated with a functioning island ecosystem. That helps explain the large differences between the restoration scenarios. Rat eradication alone produced a major projected increase from the island's current population, but restoring vegetation produced a much larger potential recovery. The model that brought the island's vegetation closer to that of nearby rat-free islands produced 138,878 breeding pairs, while the more specific one-square-kilometre conversion scenario produced 319,762. The distinction matters for conservation planners. Predator eradication can be expensive and logistically difficult, particularly on remote islands. If conservationists are going to invest that effort, the study suggests they also need to consider what happens to the landscape once the rats are gone. Otherwise, they may successfully remove the immediate threat while leaving behind a habitat that still does not provide the conditions needed for the full range of seabirds to return.What the findings could mean for other tropical islandsThe Chagos Archipelago provides a useful natural laboratory for studying this problem because many of its islands share a history of human disturbance, invasive species and coconut cultivation. But the underlying issue extends well beyond the Indian Ocean. Across tropical islands, abandoned plantations can remain long after the industries that created them have disappeared. At the same time, invasive rats and other introduced predators can continue to affect native wildlife. The combination can leave islands in a state where removing one pressure produces only part of the expected ecological recovery. The researchers' modelling suggests that island restoration should therefore be approached as an ecosystem-wide process rather than a single intervention. Rat eradication can remove one of the biggest barriers to seabird recovery, but restoring native vegetation can determine how much further that recovery goes. Ile du Coin makes the difference particularly clear. The island currently supports only 51 breeding pairs. Removing rats while leaving its existing vegetation in place could increase that figure substantially. Restoring the vegetation to resemble nearby rat-free islands raises the modelled potential dramatically further, while the more intensive conversion of one square kilometre into native forest and savannah produces the largest projection of all.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: House Dems move to block Trump’s attempted renaming of Lake Ontario
articles.summary: A trio of House Democrats introduced legislation on Monday to block President Trump from renaming Lake Ontario as “Lake America” — which he signed an executive order to do so last week amid his trade war with Canada. The legislation — titled the “Hands Off Our Great Lakes Act” — proposes prohibiting the president, Interior…
articles.body:
A trio of House Democrats introduced legislation on Monday to block President Trump from renaming Lake Ontario as “Lake America” — which he signed an executive order to do so last week amid his trade war with Canada.

The legislation — titled the “ Hands Off Our Great Lakes Act ” — proposes prohibiting the president, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and federal officials acting under presidential authority from changing the names of the five Great Lakes: Lake Superior, Lake Michigan, Lake Erie, Lake Huron and Lake Ontario.

“We filed all of the necessary papers, documents, everything else. We’ve notified all of the various people you have to notify,” the president said Thursday in the Oval Office.

The order noted the “deepest parts of the Lake’s waters” lie within U.S. territory . Lake Ontario borders New York and the Canadian province of Ontario.

Google Maps on Saturday changed the name of the body of water to Lake America on U.S. phones. The platform responded similarly to Trump’s order last year changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the “ Gulf of America .”

Democratic Reps. Debbie Dingell (Mich.), Timothy Kennedy (N.Y.) and Joseph Morelle (N.Y.) introduced the bill to block the latest move.

In addition to barring Trump from renaming any of the Great Lakes, the legislation proposed by Dingell, Kennedy and Morelle would block administration officials from using federal funds to implement the president’s executive order.

All three lawmakers blasted Trump for attempting to rename the lake, with Kennedy saying the move is “unserious” and “adds insult to injury as Trump’s tariffs drive up costs” for imported goods.

“Our families, workers, and businesses need an administration focused on lowering costs and strengthening our economy, not distractions,” Kennedy added in a joint release . “Renaming a lake won’t put food on the table, lower anyone’s bills, or create a single job. It is a pathetic attempt to distract from an affordability crisis that this President has failed to fix.”

Dingell also said preventing Trump from renaming Lake Ontario may compel the president to “turn his attention to his reckless trade war that is raising costs and threatening American workers.”

Morelle said of the president’s order, “This is ridiculous, it’s embarrassing, and it’s exactly the kind of unserious distraction Americans are tired of.”

Trump’s 50 percent import taxes on $27.6 billion worth of goods imported from Canada went into effect this month. The levies impact 5 percent of imported goods from America’s second-largest trading partner.

Canada’s “dollar for dollar” retaliatory tariffs will go into effect next week, as U.S. goods will face rates of 15, 25 or 50 percent — with the rate for each product matching the rate imposed by the Trump administration.

articles.title: Lebanon asks Greece to help enforce agreement with Israel
articles.summary: After Greece agrees to Israeli weapons deal, Joseph Aoun asks Athens to help advance US-brokered framework agreement.
articles.body:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has called for Greek help in enforcing the United States-brokered framework agreement with Israel designed to put an end to hostilities.

Aoun asked Greek President Constantine Tassoulas in a meeting on Monday to assist in facilitating an end to Israel’s occupation of areas of southern Lebanon and ongoing conflict with Lebanon-based armed group Hezbollah.

The request came hours after Greece and Israel announced a multibillion-dollar arms deal.

“We request Greece’s assistance as much as possible to help Lebanon” Aoun said in the meeting in Athens.

Lebanon and Israel signed in late June a framework agreement calling for the disarmament of Hezbollah, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from south Lebanon and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the area.

However, Hezbollah has rejected the deal unless Israel, which has continued air strikes and demolitions across southern Lebanon, first withdraws from Lebanese territory.

That leaves Beirut seeking further support to end the hostilities, insisting that it is upholding its side of the deal.

Israel has killed more than 4,300 people in Lebanon, wounded more than 12,000, and destroyed between 60 and 70 villages since March.

“Solving the problem by military force will not succeed,” Aoun warned. “The framework agreement… cannot be implemented unilaterally. It needs to be implemented on both sides,” he said.

At a press conference with Aoun, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said his country supported “the sovereignty, independence and unity of Lebanon”, and would support “all efforts aimed at de-escalation and mutual comprehension”.

Aoun said he looked forward to further Greek support.

Earlier this month, Lebanon and Israel concluded a seventh round of US-mediated talks. While negotiations were taking place in Rome, Israel escalated attacks in southern Lebanon.

The next round of talks between Israel and Lebanon is set to take place in September.

articles.title: Poland opens terror probe into fire at factory supplying Ukraine drones
articles.summary: Amid suspicion of Russian sabotage, Warsaw eyes link to foreign intelligence services.
articles.body:
Poland has opened a “terror” probe into a fire at a factory supplying parts for drones for Ukraine.

The Polish National Prosecution Office announced the launch of the investigation on Monday. While no details were offered, Russia is widely suspected of running sabotage operations across Europe against facilities supplying Ukraine as it defends itself against Moscow’s invasion.

According to the prosecution statement, the probe has been launched to investigate “participation in the activities of a foreign intelligence service directed against the Republic of Poland and for a terrorist offence, consisting of deliberately causing a fire on the premises of the WB Electronics factory using a device containing flammable materials”.

The WB Electronics factory in Skarzysko-Kamienna, located south of Warsaw, was reported to have caught fire shortly after midnight. The facility manufactures key components for drones which are supplied to the Polish and Ukrainian militaries.

Firefighters spent two hours containing the fire. The country’s Internal Security Agency is assisting the police with the investigation, officials said.

No details have been provided to the public at this stage “due to their specific and confidential nature,” an agency spokesman wrote on social media.

WB Electronics is one of Poland’s largest private defence companies. It manufactures loitering munitions, drones, fire-control systems and military-related communication tools and platforms. The Ukrainian military uses the FlyEye and Warmate drones.

A number of European countries supporting Ukraine have reported incidents that are believed to be sabotage operations by the Russians.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told reporters in August that a Russian citizen was detained “who had been recruited by Russian services to carry out assassination in Warsaw”.

In another incident, an unexploded drone was discovered at a German airport earlier in August.

Poland has been increasing its security expenditure and military capabilities due to fears of Russian attacks. WB Electronics is a key supplier to the Polish military.

articles.body: Podcaster Avi Lichtschein confronted popular children's educator Ms. Rachel about her anti-Israel comments during an interaction at a neighborhood park, according to the Sunday episode of his show, "Depends on the Context." During the episode, Lichtschein described running into the YouTuber, whose real name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, while they were both taking their children to the park. After meeting her, he asked her why she was anti-Israel. Accurso reportedly told him that she was not anti-Israel, but anti-Israeli government and anti-Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. "I pushed back on this, and I said, 'That's absurd,'" Lichtschein said. "Saying you're anti-Netanyahu, but you're not anti-Israel? Netanyahu is the democratically elected leader of the sovereign nation. I think what [she does] is way beyond that." YOUTUBE STAR MS RACHEL GIVES FUNDS TO DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL ABDUL EL-SAYED Lichtschein said that Accurso also accused Israel of committing a "genocide" through its war with Hamas. articles.title: Did LowTierGod predict his own downfall? ‘Doomsdale’ arrives as six-year streaming warning resurfaces
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Dalauan “LowTierGod,” also known as LTG, is back in the spotlight after an old comment about his streaming career resurfaced six years later. In Augus.
articles.body: Dalauan “LowTierGod,” also known as LTG, is back in the spotlight after an old comment about his streaming career resurfaced six years later. In August 2020, the fighting game creator said he would consider himself a “failure in life” if he was still primarily livestreaming six years later instead of moving into other areas such as acting. On August 30, 2026, X user @FearedBuck brought the old statement back and announced that the six-year deadline, which fans have nicknamed “Doomsdale,” had arrived. LTG has since posted a cryptic message about keeping personal dreams private.LowTierGod once said continuing to stream would mean he failedThe discussion began with an old livestream clip from August 2020. During the conversation, LTG was asked whether he expected to still be streaming six years later.He questioned why he would continue doing the same thing for that long and said his career should have moved in another direction by then.LTG said:“If I am still streaming six years later, I’m a failure. It’s just that simple. It will make no sense for me to be streaming six years later unless I had at least 500k subs.”He then explained that he did not mean he would completely stop going live. Instead, he was talking about streaming remaining his main activity without moving into other goals.LTG added:“If I am still streaming six years later, I failed in life. Quote me on that. Okay, look, no, that would be the only... I’m talking about streaming, like, now.”He went on to say that he could still livestream occasionally after achieving other goals.“When I do dope things in life, of course, I’ll still go live here and there for a while because this is where I started.”His point was that he did not want livestreaming to remain the center of his career six years into the future.That deadline has now passed, leading viewers to revisit the statement and compare it with LTG’s current career.On August 30, X user @FearedBuck posted:“Doomsdale is officially in 2 hours. Six years ago, LowTierGod said that if he was still primarily streaming instead of moving on to things like acting, he would consider himself a ‘failure in life.’”The post renewed discussion around whether LTG has reached the point he described in 2020.LowTierGod tells people to keep their dreams privateThe renewed attention came shortly after LTG shared a short message on X.On August 29, 2026, he wrote:“Never tell the world your dreams.”The post attracted more than 18.4 million views and over 63,000 likes, turning the short statement into another talking point among his followers.LTG did not directly explain whether the post was connected to his old comments about his career. He also did not publicly say whether he now considers himself to have met or missed the goals he had set in 2020.That leaves the meaning of his latest message open to interpretation. What is clear is that an old prediction he made about his future has returned to the conversation at exactly the six-year mark he originally mentioned.The discussion also shows how comments made years ago can return quickly when a creator reaches a deadline they once set for themselves. In LTG’s case, “Doomsdale” has become the name viewers use for that moment, even though the term itself came from the online discussion rather than LTG’s original statement.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Golden age of America': Trump celebrates as Supreme Court clears $400M White House ballroom
articles.summary: US News: The US Supreme Court on Monday allowed the Trump administration to continue construction of a $400 million ballroom complex at the White House, overtu.
articles.body: The US Supreme Court on Monday allowed the Trump administration to continue construction of a $400 million ballroom complex at the White House, overturning a lower-court order that had halted above-ground work while a legal challenge against the project proceeds.The 5-4 decision was a victory for Trump, who has pushed ahead with the project despite a lawsuit arguing that the president does not have the authority to undertake such a major alteration to the White House complex without congressional approval.The court’s unsigned order did not rule definitively on whether the ballroom itself is lawful. Instead, it found that the National Trust for Historic Preservation, the group challenging the project, likely lacked the legal standing to bring the case and said the government could face "irreparable harm" if construction were stopped.The decision was backed by five of the court’s six conservative justices. Chief Justice John Roberts dissented, joining the court’s three liberal justices.In a strongly worded dissent, Roberts argued that the ruling did not resolve the central legal question and said the ballroom was "likely unlawful" because Congress had not expressly authorised its construction.Roberts pointed to federal law governing construction on federal parkland and public grounds in Washington, arguing that Congress has authority over federal property in the capital."Today’s decision is no victory for the separation of powers," he wrote, as reported by the Associated Press.The National Trust for Historic Preservation had argued that Trump lacked unilateral authority to demolish the White House's East Wing and replace it with a 90,000-square-foot ballroom.Lower courts had previously agreed that construction should be halted above ground while the legal challenge continued. A federal appeals court upheld that order earlier this month, saying the president could not fundamentally reshape the White House without congressional approval.Trump hails Supreme Court rulingTrump welcomed the decision, calling the lawsuit "baseless" and celebrating what he described as a victory for his ballroom and wider military complex."I am pleased to report that the United States Supreme Court has just ruled in favor of the Ballroom/Military Complex being built without any further contingency, doubt, or threat," Trump said in a post on Truth Social.The administration has defended the project not only as an expansion of the White House but also as a national security measure. Justice Department lawyers told the Supreme Court that the complex would include a highly secure ballroom linked to an underground military installation.Trump has said the underground complex will include bomb shelters, medical facilities and protection against drones and missiles. The administration has argued that stopping construction could compromise security arrangements at the White House.The project was initially presented as a privately funded ballroom, but national security became a central argument in the administration's legal defence after courts ordered construction to stop.East Wing already demolishedThe administration demolished the White House East Wing, which had housed the first lady's offices and a White House movie theatre, to make way for the new complex.Trump has described the planned ballroom as the "greatest" of its kind and said it would be completed in 2028. Court documents cited by the AP said construction crews were working up to 20 hours a day, with the framework expected to be completed in November and much of the exterior by April.The administration has said the broader East Wing project, including underground facilities, is already about 65% complete.The National Trust, however, has accused the White House of attempting to accelerate construction and "outrun the courts" before the legal battle over the project's authority is resolved.The Supreme Court's Monday order allows construction to continue for now, but the underlying legal dispute over Trump's authority to build the ballroom without Congress remains unresolved.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Navy unveils ‘MALICE’ missile built to strike enemy aircraft from extreme range
articles.summary: Raytheon is developing a new 1,500-pound long-range missile, the AIM-424 LRAAM, to extend the reach and survivability of Navy and Marine aviators.
articles.body: The U.S. Navy is developing a brand-new, extra-long-range missile designed to shoot down enemy aircraft before they can get close enough to threaten American fighter jets or aircraft carriers. The department announced the new weapon on Aug. 22, saying the next-generation AIM-424 LRAAM is nicknamed "MALICE." The weapon is designed to be fired from a jet to target enemy aircraft or drones at extreme distances in the air. In practice, American pilots will be able to detect an enemy on radar, launch the missile from extreme ranges and destroy the target before coming within close proximity to the enemy, potentially increasing the pilot's survivability. ARMY CONDUCTS FIRST OVERSEAS TEST OF 'HAMMER OF THE GODS' WEAPON-DISRUPTING SYSTEM "LRAAM sustains the Department’s first look, first shot, first kill advantage by providing our aviators greater reach, greater survivability, and greater tactical flexibility in the air-to-air fight," the Navy said. The missile is designed to increase the "range, lethality, and combat effectiveness for Marine and Naval aviation forces," officials added. EUROPE'S $116B FIGHTER JET 'FAILURE' RAISES FRESH DOUBTS ABOUT ABILITY TO DEFEND ITSELF WITHOUT US Its range is listed as "in excess" of 250 nautical miles, or roughly 287 statute miles. That is a massive distance for an air-to-air missile, allowing jets to protect an entire fleet from far over the horizon. At 13.5 feet long and weighing 1,500 pounds, the missile is significantly larger and heavier than standard medium-range air-to-air missiles. In comparison, the AIM-120 AMRAAM weighs about 335 pounds, underscoring the size of the propulsion system needed to propel the LRAAM to extreme distances. The missile is also equipped with a blast-fragmentation warhead, meaning it does not necessarily have to score a direct physical hit. Instead, it detonates near the target, sending fragments outward to destroy or disable the aircraft. Officials said the missile is compatible with aircraft across multiple generations, including fourth and fifth-generation fighters as well as future sixth-generation aircraft. articles.title: Three minors killed in Colombia armed group crackdown
articles.summary: Rights groups warn that armed groups are increasingly recruiting children to their ranks through social media.
articles.body:
Three minors were among those killed in a Colombian military air strike on cocaine-trafficking rebels last week, authorities said, as President Abelardo de la Espriella intensifies operations against armed groups.

The August 27 bombing in the southern Guaviare department was the deadliest military operation since de la Espriella took office earlier this month. The National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences said that 10 people in total were killed in the operation. The Ministry of National Defence reported that two of the victims were 15 and another was 16.

The victims allegedly belonged to a dissident faction of the defunct Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, or FARC, that rejected a 2016 peace agreement with the government.

De la Espriella, a right-wing leader and ally of United States President Donald Trump, said on Monday that another bombing in the same area killed eight members of a FARC dissident group led by commander Ivan Mordisco. It is not known whether any minors were among the dead.

“The bandits, who for decades have recruited minors to turn them into combatants or human shields, must pay for these crimes that violate International Humanitarian Law,” he wrote on X.

The Defence Ministry said on Monday that 24 suspected rebels have been killed in military operations since de la Espriella took office.

The strikes come as child recruitment by armed groups is again rising in Colombia, according to a Human Rights Watch (HRW) report published last week.

At least 1,500 children have been recruited by armed groups since 2021, with 625 cases reported in 2024, according to the report.

The watchdog said that criminal and rebel groups are using social media to recruit children, including to carry out increasingly dangerous tasks, such as operating drones loaded with explosives. They also reported that algorithms on platforms including Meta and TikTok “appear to have actively promoted” content encouraging children to join rebel groups.

“Armed groups in Colombia are recruiting children with impunity,” said Juanita Goebertus, HRW’s Americas director. “Protection systems are failing, and social media platforms have become a more effective recruiting ground.”

Meta and TikTok told HRW that they prohibit content promoting violence and had removed accounts flagged by the organisation.

articles.title: Florida bans Flock and other license plate readers from state highways
articles.summary: Florida’s state transportation office revoked the ability of local police to put license plate readers on state highways.
articles.body: Florida’s state transportation office on Monday revoked the ability of local police to put license plate readers on state highways, as a nationwide backlash continued to gain steam against Flock Safety and other makers of surveillance cameras. Will Watts, the chief operating officer of the Florida Department of Transportation, informed local law enforcement agencies in a one-page memo that the department was revoking all previously issued approvals for license plate readers (LPRs) in state “rights-of-way,” or the strip of land that’s next to or part of a state road. Watts cited a “recent exponential increase” in deployments of law enforcement cameras, as well as “concerning reports of misuse, data privacy concerns, and surveillance schemes” that he said merit immediate action “to preserve Floridians’ sovereignty and quality of life.” Automatic license plate cameras are mounted to surveil roads throughout the United States, recording which vehicles pass by and when, often with the goal of catching criminal suspects or developing leads. The technology has been around since the 1970s but has spread widely in the past few years as the software has improved and the cost of hardware has fallen. Flock provides a network to customers that allows law enforcement groups from across the country to share footage from their cameras with other agencies and departments, prompting concerns about abuse. The memo fulfills a vow from Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, a Republican, who last week said that surveillance had gone too far. “We’re gonna clear the state right-of-ways,” he said Friday on the Real America’s Voice podcast. “These cameras that are out there now — who’s to say they’re only doing the license plate?” he said. “Now, they say that. I think it’s capturing people in their cars. I think it’s capturing way more information than they’re letting on. And you’ve seen the abuse.” Florida is not alone. Last week, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, a Republican, ordered a halt to state funding for Flock cameras, according to The Texas Tribune, and the issue has come up in midterm election campaigns. More than 100 local governments have canceled or not renewed their LPR contracts since the beginning of last year, according to the Institute for Justice, an advocacy group in Virginia that says the technology is unconstitutional. Monday’s order did not affect cameras on private property or on local rights-of-way — where 98% of the surveillance cameras are located, DeSantis said — but some localities in Florida said they were following suit. The Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office said it would discontinue the use of license plate reader technology throughout its jurisdiction, Duval County, “effective immediately” even as it called the technology “an enormously valuable investigative tool.” The county, which includes Jacksonville, has 1 million residents. Flock Safety, which in recent years has helped to popularize license plate readers and other camera technology for police departments, said that a ban was the wrong reaction. “Flock’s technology is an important public safety tool for law enforcement agencies across Florida, helping officers solve serious crimes, find missing people, recover stolen vehicles, and support safer communities,” the company said in a statement. “In just the last few weeks in Florida, the technology was used to find missing children, led to the arrest of a murder suspect, and assisted in solving numerous other crimes,” it said, pointing to local news coverage of its cameras’ impact. “Rather than banning a critical public safety tool, we support thoughtful legislation and strong privacy, transparency, and accountability guardrails that ensure technology is used responsibly while preserving law enforcement’s ability to use effective tools to keep people safe,” the company said. The company has announced changes in recent weeks in response to privacy concerns, including shrinking the period for how long it holds people’s movement data by default from one month to one week. It also has said it will do more to lock out users whose searches display “abnormal activity.” Last week, a Kentucky police officer was arrested after authorities said he used the Flock system more than 2,000 times to track his ex-girlfriend. NBC News has identified 50 areas across the country where Flock cameras have been damaged, spray-painted, smashed or cut down in acts of vandalism since 2024, while some drivers have sued Flock and organized themselves into a proposed class action.

articles.summary: Democratic Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed appeared to defend his criticism of Fourth of July fireworks on "The Breakfast Club" radio show.
articles.body: Democratic Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed defended his past controversial comments about Fourth of July fireworks during a radio appearance Monday. While appearing on "The Breakfast Club," El-Sayed was asked by host Charlamagne tha God about his previous support for defunding the police and criticism of firework celebrations on Independence Day. You don't have a complete conception of America. But even then, right, like what is it?'" WASHINGTON POST THROWS COLD WATER ON DC FIREWORKS WITH REPORT OF ‘HAZARDOUS AIR POLLUTION’ He continued: "I said, 'Well, every time we do a fireworks show, it destroys the air quality and people have asthma exacerbations and heart attacks the next day.' SOCIALIST CANDIDATES CAN DELETE OLD POSTS, BUT THEY CAN'T ERASE THEIR RADICALISM The video allegedly included four reasons "why fireworks suck" and a chapter titled "Fireworks just aren't worth it: hear us out." articles.title: Summer 2026 expected to be declared UK's hottest on record
articles.summary: Met Office figures due on Tuesday are likely to show that the previous record, set in 2025, has been broken after an unprecedented summer of persistent heat.
articles.body:
The Met Office is expected to confirm that the UK has had its hottest summer since records began in 1884.

Provisional figures for the months of June, July and August are due to be released on Tuesday afternoon and are likely to reveal that mean temperatures - which include daytime and overnight values - have broken the previous record, set just last year .

It follows a spring and summer of persistent heat with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days of temperatures above 30C (86F), smashing the previous record of 34 days.

The temperature figures are in line with evidence that summers are getting hotter , with more intense and frequent heatwaves, as a result of human-induced climate change. Records are being broken more often - and by bigger margins.

Record summer likely despite a cooler end to August

For much of the summer, areas of high pressure have dominated the UK weather, with dry conditions and winds from continental Europe allowing temperatures to rise repeatedly.

On 11 August the Met Office said it was looking increasingly likely to be the hottest summer since records began.

The UK's mean temperature for the summer up to that point stood at 16.48C (61.66F), with only average conditions needed during the remainder of August to confirm the seasonal record.

The second half of the month did bring a change in the pattern with cooler, wetter weather for many - but overall temperatures have mostly remained around or above the seasonal norm.

Some variations are expected in the final figures for the four UK nations.

England and Wales are both expected to set new records, Northern Ireland is likely to come close - but Scotland will fall short.

The highest temperature recorded this summer was 38.1C (100.6F) at Kew Gardens in London on 13 August.

This was, provisionally, the UK's fifth-hottest day on record in terms of maximum temperature, but it didn't meet the all-time high of 40.3C (104.5F) measured at Coningsby, Lincolnshire in July 2022.

However, it is the persistence of the heat this spring and summer that is remarkable and has broken numerous records.

A temperature of 30C or higher has been recorded on 40 separate days. The previous record was 34 days, set in 1995.

A temperature of 35C or higher has been recorded on 10 separate days. The previous record was five days, set in 1976 and matched in 2020.

A temperature of 35C or higher was recorded in four calendar months - May, June, July and August. The previous record was two calendar months.

A temperature of 37C or higher has been recorded on three separate days, which is a new record. 37C+ has only been recorded nine times in the UK - three of which have occurred this year.

There have been five widespread heatwaves , including one at the end of meteorological spring which broke the UK's May temperature record by more than 2C.

Another in June broke the temperature record for that month too - with Lingwood, Norfolk reaching 38.0C on 26 June. The previous June high was 35.6C, in the historic summer of 1976.

July and August brought further heatwaves - including one that lasted for three weeks in some locations and another which delivered the highest temperature of the year .

The intense heat occurred partly because of how dry it was for much of the summer - with some areas seeing no measurable rainfall for more than two months , external .

Drought was declared in all of Wales and more than two-thirds of England and wildfires caused devastation in parts of the country.

However, rain did fall in early June and wet weather returned in the second half of August, bringing some flash flooding .

Sheffield recorded over a month's worth of rain in the week of 24-30 August - more than the city had seen across the rest of the season combined.

This summer is not expected to break any records for dryness across the UK as a whole.

UK weather is now happening in a warming climate

There is something striking about the way the UK's summer temperature record is being broken.

In a climate that isn't changing, new records should generally become progressively rarer, because every time a record falls, it raises the bar for the next one.

Instead, all five of the UK's hottest summers on record have occurred since 2000 , external . And until last year, the margins between them were tiny: the four hottest were separated by just five hundredths of a degree.

Then came 2025. The record jumped by 0.34C. Now, just a year later, it looks like that record has gone too.

"Record-shattering" sounds like the kind of language we journalists would use. In fact, it is a term climate scientists use for records broken by unusually large margins. Research suggests , external these big jumps become more likely if the climate is warming rapidly.

So why is this happening so quickly here? The UK sits on the western edge of Europe, the fastest-warming continent on Earth - warming at roughly twice the global rate.

There are a few reasons for that. Land heats up faster than the oceans, parts of Europe stretch into the rapidly warming Arctic, and changes in weather patterns have favoured more frequent and intense summer heatwaves.

Scientists are still working out exactly how much each factor contributes, but the result is clear: the background climate in which British weather happens is getting warmer.

None of this means the UK will break its summer record every year. Weather will always give us cooler summers as well as hotter ones. But the pattern is becoming unmistakable: records that once marked the extreme edge of the UK's climate are being overtaken with remarkable speed.

So the question is not whether the UK will experience summers hotter than this one. It is how often they will come - and how much hotter they might be.
